gaps.title: Award Package is enabled on a package with no quotes attached
gaps.description: The user decided the awarded supplier is chosen from the quotes attached to the package (DEC-001 verbatim). The captured PKG-104 page shows 'No quotes attached yet.' while the Award Package button is enabled. It is not defined whether awarding must be blocked, warned or otherwise handled when no quotes are attached.

evidence_refs.locator: SCR-012 actions Award Package visibly_disabled false
ambiguous_behaviours SCR-012 'Can a package be awarded with no quotes attached'

gaps.why_it_matters: Awards are final and cannot be undone (DEC-002), so an award made with no eligible quote cannot be corrected afterwards.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The spec could allow an irreversible award with no supplier eligible under the customer's own rule, or the mockup and spec will contradict each other.

gaps.title: No way to choose which supplier receives the award
gaps.description: REQ-001 requires awarding a package to one supplier, chosen from attached quotes (DEC-001). The award form shows only an Award note field and an Award Package button; no supplier choice is shown in the capture, and the package already displays a Supplier field whose relation to the awarded supplier is not explained.
gaps.why_it_matters: The central must-have of this feature, awarding to one supplier, is not supported by any captured screen element, and the existing Supplier field on the package makes it unclear whether the supplier is already fixed before award.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The award step cannot be specified; the wrong supplier could be awarded irreversibly.

gaps.title: Who may award, and who may see which packages
gaps.description: REQ-001 names package managers as able to award, but it is not stated whether any other role may award, whether a package manager may award any package or only their own, or how the product distinguishes package managers from other users. Who can see which packages in the list is also not stated. The capture shows no role or signed-in user.

evidence_refs.locator: REQ-001 ambiguity_notes 'Whether other roles may also award is not stated.'
ambiguous_behaviours SCR-012 'Who is allowed to award a package?'
ambiguous_behaviours SCR-007 'Who can see which packages?'

gaps.why_it_matters: An award is final and triggers an email to suppliers, so who can perform it directly controls the risk of unauthorised or mistaken commitments to a supplier.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Permissions for the irreversible action cannot be specified; unauthorised users might award packages or see packages they should not.

gaps.title: Outcome of pressing Award Package is not shown
gaps.description: The Award Package button has no target in the capture. What happens after pressing it is not shown in the capture: the loading state, the success state, failure states, whether the user stays on the page, and whether status changes to Awarded with a recorded date as seen on PKG-105.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-012 'what is shown on success or failure?'

gaps.why_it_matters: The award is the core workflow of this feature and is irreversible; users need to know whether it succeeded, and a failed or partial award must not leave the package in an unclear state.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The main workflow ends in an unspecified state; users may retry an award they think failed, or believe an award succeeded when it did not.
research_questions: What are established patterns for communicating success and failure of an irreversible, server-confirmed action in procurement or approval workflows?
How should partial failure be presented when a record update succeeds but a follow-on step (such as sending an email) fails?

gaps.title: No confirmation shown before an irreversible award
gaps.description: The user decided an award cannot be undone by anyone (DEC-002). The capture shows no confirmation step before awarding; whether one exists and what it must show (for example the supplier and value being committed) is not defined.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-012 'Is there a confirmation step'

gaps.why_it_matters: With no undo and no correction path, a single accidental press of Award Package locks the package for everyone and notifies suppliers.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Accidental or mistaken awards become permanent with no recovery.
research_questions: What do usability guidelines (for example GOV.UK Design System or Nielsen Norman Group) recommend for confirming irreversible actions that cannot be undone?
What information should a confirmation for committing a contract award to a supplier display?

gaps.title: Duplicate and concurrent award attempts
gaps.description: It is not defined what happens if Award Package is pressed twice, a request is retried, or two package managers award the same package at the same time, possibly to different suppliers, or while another user still has the Open view loaded.
gaps.why_it_matters: A package may be awarded to only one supplier and awards are final, so a double or conflicting award cannot be corrected, and duplicate emails could reach suppliers.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Two irreversible awards or repeated supplier notifications for one package.
research_questions: What are established techniques for making a one-time state transition (such as awarding) idempotent and safe against double submission?
How do web applications typically detect and report that a record was changed by another user while a stale view was open?

gaps.title: Notification recipients and content are undefined
gaps.description: DEC-004 sets email at the time of award, but its verbatim says 'Suppliers are notified', while the interpretation records only the winning supplier; whether unsuccessful quoting suppliers are also notified is unresolved. Email content, and where each supplier's email address comes from, are not stated; the capture shows only a supplier name.
gaps.why_it_matters: REQ-003 is a must-have and is still marked unknown; the email is the supplier's only stated signal that they won, and notifying the wrong set of suppliers has commercial consequences.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The notification cannot be specified; unsuccessful suppliers may be left uninformed or informed incorrectly, and the email may lack what the supplier needs to act.
research_questions: What information do award notification emails in supplier procurement typically contain for winning and unsuccessful bidders?

Are there common regulatory expectations (for example UK Procurement Act 2023 or EU public procurement directives) for notifying unsuccessful bidders, and do they apply to private-sector supplier packages?

gaps.title: Email delivery failure after an award
gaps.description: It is not defined what happens if the award email cannot be sent or bounces: who is told, whether it is retried, and whether the award still stands.
gaps.why_it_matters: The award is final regardless of delivery, so a silent email failure leaves a winning supplier unaware with no visible signal to the package manager.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Suppliers may never learn they won; REQ-003 is not met with nobody aware.
research_questions: What are common practices for detecting, retrying and surfacing failed or bounced transactional emails?

gaps.title: Traceability of who awarded and when
gaps.description: The awarded page shows an award date but no awarding user; the awarding user is only inferred. Whether the award must be recorded with who, when, which supplier, the note and the quote it was based on, and who may view that record, is not stated.

evidence_refs.locator: SCR-030 fields Awarding user basis inferred

gaps.why_it_matters: Awards commit the business to a supplier and cannot be reversed, so disputes about who awarded and on what basis can only be settled from the record.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Awards could not be attributed or justified later.
research_questions: What fields do procurement audit trails typically record for a contract award decision?

gaps.title: Award note rules and where the note appears
gaps.description: The Award note field has no visible required marker; whether it is required, optional or length-limited, what validation messages appear, and whether the note is shown on the awarded package or in the supplier email are not stated. The captured PKG-105 page does not show a note.

evidence_refs.locator: SCR-012 fields Award note required_marker_visible false
ambiguous_behaviours SCR-012 'Is the Award note required, optional, or length-limited?'

gaps.why_it_matters: Once awarded, all fields are locked for everyone (DEC-003), so the note cannot be corrected later and its audience matters if suppliers see it.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Notes may be missing, truncated or exposed to suppliers unintentionally, with no way to fix them.

gaps.title: How quotes are attached and what they contain
gaps.description: DEC-001 makes attached quotes the basis for supplier choice, but the Quotes section is only shown empty. How quotes are attached, by whom, what a quote contains, and whether quotes are locked after award are not shown in the capture.

evidence_refs.locator: SCR-031 fields Quote contents basis inferred

gaps.why_it_matters: The award depends on quotes, so without knowing what a quote holds (supplier, amount) the eligible suppliers and the award step cannot be defined.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Award eligibility under DEC-001 cannot be specified or tested.

gaps.title: Package status values and which allow award
gaps.description: Only Open and Awarded are shown. Other status values, their transitions, and which statuses permit awarding are not stated.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-007 'What are all the possible Status values and their transitions?'

gaps.why_it_matters: Whether the award button is enabled and when the read-only lock applies both depend on package status.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Packages in unlisted states could be awarded or locked incorrectly.

gaps.title: Accessibility of the disabled award button and award status messages
gaps.description: On PKG-105 the Award Package button is disabled with no visible explanation in the capture, and how the award result would be announced to assistive technology is not shown.
gaps.why_it_matters: The read-only state is communicated only through a disabled button, and the award outcome is critical feedback for an irreversible action; both must be perceivable to all users.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Users relying on assistive technology may not understand why they cannot act or whether an award succeeded.
research_questions: What does WCAG 2.2 AA (including SC 4.1.3 Status Messages) require for announcing the result of a form submission?
What are accessible practices for disabled buttons, including explaining why an action is unavailable?

gaps.title: Retention and deletion of locked awarded packages
gaps.description: Awarded packages are locked for everyone (DEC-003). Whether an awarded package, its quotes or its award record can ever be deleted or archived, and how long they are retained, is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: A lock for everyone conflicts with any later need to remove or archive records, which this product has not addressed.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Awarded records may accumulate indefinitely or be removed in ways that break the lock.

gaps.title: Package list search, sorting and paging behaviour
gaps.description: Which fields search matches, when it applies, what is shown for no results, and whether the table is sortable, filterable or paginated are not shown in the capture.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-007 'Is the table sortable, filterable or paginated?'

gaps.why_it_matters: The list is the only captured entry point to a package's award page, so package managers depend on it to find the right package.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Search and list behaviour will be decided ad hoc during build.

gaps.title: Award date, currency and time zone formats
gaps.description: The award date is shown as '2 Oct 2026' and packages show a value; the currency, the date format, and which time zone defines the award date are not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: The award date is a permanent record and may appear in supplier emails, so an ambiguous date or currency could mislead suppliers.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Recorded award dates or values may be misread across regions.

gaps.title: Reports screen content and link to awards
gaps.description: The Reports screen shows only 'Coming soon.'; whether it relates to awards, what it would contain and who may access it is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Reports are reachable from every captured screen and are named as a possible downstream effect of awarding, so scope for this feature is unclear.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: It stays unclear whether awards must feed reports in this feature.

assumptions.text: The verbatim of DEC-001 ('The supplier is chosen from the quotes attached to the package.') is taken as the user's answer, rather than its interpretation 'Only suppliers are eligible.'
assumptions.why: The recorded interpretation does not reflect the verbatim answer, and the verbatim is the user's own words.
assumptions.impact: GAP-001, GAP-002 and GAP-011 treat attached quotes as the basis for supplier eligibility.
assumptions.to_confirm: That eligible suppliers are those whose quotes are attached to the package.

assumptions.text: 'Package managers' in REQ-001 is a distinct user role in the product.
assumptions.why: No role or signed-in user is shown in the capture.
assumptions.impact: GAP-003 assumes roles exist to distinguish who may award.
assumptions.to_confirm: Whether the product has user roles and which ones exist.

assumptions.text: The disabled Award Package button on PKG-105 reflects its Awarded status rather than the viewer's permissions.
assumptions.why: The capture does not explain why the button is disabled.
assumptions.impact: GAP-012 and GAP-013 treat the disabled button as the read-only state of REQ-002.
assumptions.to_confirm: Why the button is disabled on awarded packages.

proposed_status_changes.reason: How the awarded supplier is selected is not supported by the mockup, and whether award is allowed with no quotes attached contradicts DEC-001 (GAP-001, GAP-002).
DEC-004 verbatim says 'Suppliers' while its interpretation says only the winning supplier; recipients need confirming (GAP-007).
